newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian meat firms urge end to pork import tax.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian meat firms urge end to pork import tax.

text.p: Bulgarian meat processors said on Monday the government should remove import duties on pork to increase competition and improve quality.

"It is ridiculous to have a domestic wholesale price of $2,500 per tonne of pork when international prices are around $1,200-$1,400," said Georgi Georgiev, executive director of the Association of Bulgarian Meat Processors. The import duty on pork is $800 per tonne.
"Pig breeders are seeing the import duty as a shelter and they are pushing up prices because of the shortage of pork in the market," Georgiev told a news conference.
Alexander Ivanov, director of private meat processing firm Caritex, said high meat prices were forcing sausage producers to use non-meat additives.
The meat processors' association said it planned to introduce a quality trademark to guarantee basic quality standards for consumers.

"We are planning to work together with the fodder producers and the agriculture ministry to achieve transparency in the whole process of meat processing. Through free market competition we hope to secure good quality production at affordable prices," Georgiev said.
